title: AZ egress gateway allocator and conditional PrivateLink routing
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Introduces AZ-aware egress gateway allocator and optional PrivateLink routing per-subnet tag. Backwards compatible defaults; rollout requires terraform plan and operator upgrade. Improves cross-AZ failover stability and reduces NAT cost churn.
description:
Motivation: Customers with multi-AZ private control planes saw elevated egress cost and transient routing flips when NAT pools or PrivateLink endpoints were rebalanced. This change introduces an AZ-aware egress gateway allocator and a conditional PrivateLink routing mode that creates PrivateLink endpoints only for subnets tagged as "redwood:privatelink=true". The allocator pins egress assignments to AZ-local gateway instances where capacity permits, falls back gracefully to cross-AZ gateways when required, and exposes a deterministic allocation table so rollout and troubleshooting are reproducible.

What this PR does (single-string description): Adds a controller (egress_allocator) that reconciles EgressGateway CRs, selects AZ-local gateway resources, and writes assignment annotations. Adds a privatelink_router controller that can create/delete PrivateLink endpoints based on subnet tags and route table annotations. Adds Terraform module changes to support named egress pools, EIP rotation policies, and per-AZ affinity tags. Updates Helm templates to expose allocator feature-flag and health/readiness metrics. Adds integration tests that simulate AZ failover and verify allocator stability and minimal route churn. Adds docs with a step-by-step migration and an upgrade/rollback playbook.

Migration and rollout notes: Default behavior is backward compatible — allocator is disabled unless featureFlag. To enable: update charts/values-private.yaml to set allocator.enabled=true, apply Terraform to provision per-AZ named pools, and upgrade installer controller. Migration steps included in docs/private/egress-migration.md and a canary plan for small clusters. Rollback is handled by controller draining and releasing assignments; Terraform module preserves existing NAT gateways unless explicitly replaced.

Commits (high level):
- 7c1a2d2: add egress allocator controller scaffolding and API types
- 2d9f4a1: implement deterministic AZ affinity algorithm and assignment reconciliation
- a117b8c: terraform: add egress-gateway module with named pool support and EIP rotation policy
- b3f4e22: helm: expose allocator flags, probe endpoints, and metrics
- 49c12f0: privatelink_router controller with tag-driven endpoint lifecycle
- 8d7a901: integration tests for AZ failover and route stability
- 0f4b8c3: docs and migration playbook

Files changed (high-level): Terraform module adds new variables for az_affinity_weight and eip_pool_policy; Helm chart gains allocator.enabled, allocator.metricsPort, and privatelink.routingMode flags; controller adds two new CRDs (EgressGateway, EgressAssignment) and two controllers. Tests include simulated AZ outage harness and assertions on route-table modifications.

Examples and snippets: allocator computes a weighted score for candidate gateways and pins assignments via annotation: "redwood.io/egress-assignment: gateway-az-a-0001". PrivateLink creation is gated by subnet tag and only proceeds if the subnet's route table has the 'egress://managed' tag.

CI and testing: CI ran integration pipeline (ci/pipeline/egress-integration.yml) with creation of 3 simulated AZs; one flaky test (route-flap-detect) initially failed and was retried, subsequent runs passed. Unit tests cover allocator algorithm edge-cases.

Review summary and decisions: After feedback on deterministic tie-breakers and API naming we settled on deterministic assignment tables and kept EgressAssignment as a namespaced CRD rather than cluster-scoped to simplify RBAC. We also chose to make PrivateLink routing opt-in via a subnet tag to avoid surprising customers who manage endpoints externally.

Related work: builds on ENG-7123 (egress cost stabilization) and SRE-314 (private control plane routing hardening).

Merge notes: Squash merge after green pipelines; Terraform module bump requires a follow-on apply in infra to create named pools. Manual verification checklist is included in docs/private/egress-migration.md.
review_comments: Elliot Chen: Please ensure allocator is idempotent across controller restarts; observed a race when multiple controllers reconcile same EgressGateway.
Maya Patel (reply): Added optimistic locking via annotation version and test that tears down/restarts controller; included in allocator_test.go.
Rina Kaur: Can we gate PrivateLink creation behind a feature flag and subnet tag? I don't want implicit endpoint creation.
Maya Patel (reply): PrivateLink creation is gated by both charts.values and 'redwood:privatelink=true' subnet tag per review; updated docs to call this out.
Samir Patel: Terraform change will create named EIP pools — add migration plan so existing NATs are preserved.
Maya Patel (reply): Included migration steps and a non-destructive default that preserves untagged NATs; added a migration playbook in docs.
Elliot Chen (approval): Approving pending one small linter nit fix (done).
